claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria was an early Christian theologian and ascetic who lived circa 185–253 CE and served as head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria.
In the early third century Origen composed a series of homilies on the Book of Job, known as the Enarrationes in Job or Homiliae in Job.
Scholars date the extant fragments of Origen’s Job commentary to around the year 245 CE.
The commentary is significant because it represents the earliest systematic treatment of the Book of Job by a church father, shaping later patristic exegesis of the text.
Origen’s interpretation introduced the image of Job as a patient athlete wrestling the devil, a motif that became central in later Christian devotion to Job.
